name: Null Signal // Static City Tour Tee
description:
Null Signal is a post-industrial noise collective out of the Shelf's lower grid — three musicians, a rotating cast of sound designers, and a visual artist named Yolanda Ferris who does all their merch by hand-screening in batches of forty or fifty at a time. The Static City Tour Tee is the shirt from their 2199 run through six underground venues across the Chicago-Milwaukee corridor. The design is a dense overlapping cityscape rendered in grainy halftone — the kind that reads as abstraction from a distance and resolves into the silhouette of the Spire as you get closer. Printed in silver ink on a black heavyweight cotton-analog tee.

The printing is slightly uneven — Ferris doesn't sweat registration errors — and the silver has a subtle metallic quality that catches light in dim venues. The shirt is cut boxy and runs a size large. Most people wearing it either saw the shows or know someone who did. A small number are just fans who traded for one online. It's been bootlegged twice, both times noticeably worse.
what_it_says: You were in the room. Or you at least know what rooms matter.
manufacturer: Null Signal (independent — Yolanda Ferris, screen printer)
story_hooks: One of the forty-three shirts from the first night's batch was printed on a shirt that already had something written on the inside collar — in a language the band doesn't recognize.
Null Signal's lead vocalist went missing two weeks after the tour ended. The shirt has become something of a memorial object in certain circles.
A Tier 4 streetwear label wants to license the Static City design for a collaboration. Ferris has not responded to any messages.
